To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have measured the half-lives, α branching ratios and α-decay energies of the neutron-deficient isotopes 200,201,202,203,204Fr and 197At and the half-lives and α branching ratios of the neutron-deficit isotopes 199,201,202At and 199Fr.
the 200Fr half-life is substantially longer than previously thought, and that the 196At half-life is substantially shorter than previously thought.
the half-life of 200Fr is substantially shorter than previously assumed and that the 196At half-life is substantially longer than previously assumed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the decay properties of the most neutron deficient isotopes of francium and astatine.
the study of the α-decay chains of the neutron-deficient isotopes of Fr and At.
the study of the heaviest known isotopes of the elements from Fr to At.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

all these nuclei are very neutron deficient, and that the α-decay of 200Fr is a very fast one, with an extremely low Qα value, which is the most probable explanation for the discrepancy with the earlier literature data.
the α decay of the 200,202,204,206Fr isotopes is hindered by the formation of a 4p-1h shell closure, and that the α-decay hindrance factor is about 2.5 times larger than the one for 204Fr.
the α decay half-life of 200Fr is 49(4 ms), the α decay half-live of 196At is 389(54 ms), and that the α decay of 196,198,200At is energetically allowed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 196, 198At half-lives are longer than previously thought, while the half-lives for the lighter At isotopes are substantially shorter.
the half-lives for the 200Fr and 198, 199, 201Fr α-decays, and the α branching ratio for the 196At α-decay are now known with a much improved accuracy.
all measured half-lives are shorter than those reported in the literature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the half-life of 200Fr has been measured for the first time, and the results for all other nuclei have been improved significantly.
the α-decay properties of neutron-deficient isotopes are not well described by the standard α-decay model.
the α decay of 200Fr is faster than expected from systematics and that the α decay is not the dominant decay mode for 196At.
